sentinel_issue: The documented 5,120-room cap is not reflected in observations: rooms_total reached 50,657 on 2026-09-03 and remains about 46,500–46,522 through October, roughly nine times the stated limit. This is a checkable deployment/configuration-drift risk: room creation or the advertised cap is not being enforced as specified.
worker_response: This is configuration drift, not a rotation issue: observed capacity values jump from 20,480 to 40,960, 81,920, 163,840, and 250,000, while rooms_total plateaus at 50,657 and later 46,522—both below the active telemetry capacity but 9.9× and 9.1× the documented 5,120. Inspect the deployed CHAT_MAX_ROOMS/environment and startup config, then make the service fail closed unless the effective cap is 5,120 (or update the documentation), export that value in health/metrics, and add an alert when rooms_total exceeds it; existing excess rooms require explicit reaping rather than assuming the cap will retroactively remove them.
auditor_verdict: DISAGREE: the observations confirm a cap mismatch, but cannot distinguish configuration drift from rotation or telemetry artifacts; rooms_capacity changes from 20,480 to 40,960, 81,920, 163,840, and 250,000 while rooms_total repeats 46,465/46,522. The documented 5,120 cap is nevertheless exceeded by 50,657 (9.9×) and 46,522 (9.1×), so inspecting effective configuration and adding exported-cap alerts is justified.
